body: New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 18 provides that the appropriate New Zealand superannuation rate for a person who is living alone and entitled under section 17(2)(a) or (b) as the spouse or partner of a person in long-term residential care in a hospital or rest home is the single living alone rate.

New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 section 19 applies hospital rates to a married, civil union, or de facto person with no dependent children, or to a single person, who receives or becomes entitled to New Zealand superannuation. The rate is not affected for a hospital period of 13 weeks or less. For more than 13 weeks, from the 14th week the rate is the Schedule 1 clause 3 rate, unless a Residential Care and Disability Support Services Act funder is paying some or all contracted care costs. If a partnered person's superannuation is reduced, the spouse or partner's specified benefit is increased by the difference between the maximum single rate and the maximum partnered rate with a spouse receiving superannuation, unless the spouse or partner is also in hospital for more than 13 weeks. If the hospitalised superannuitant is absent from hospital for not more than 28 days, the rate on return is determined as if the absence had not occurred.

New Zealand Superannuation and Retirement Income Act 2001 Schedule 1 Part 2 sets rates saved by Schedule 1AA before deduction of tax. For a person whose spouse or partner is not entitled to New Zealand superannuation or a veteran's pension, clause 1(a) gives $984.28 a week subject to Income Test 3 for the pre-1 October 1991 alternative-rate case or the paragraph (b) rate, whichever is greater. Clause 1(b) gives $933.16 a week subject to Income Test 3 in any other case.
